summary.headline: Prince Pipes Q2 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR821 crores and EBITDA 82% to INR100 crores at a 12% margin, with management reaffirming an 11-13% margin band.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR821 crores (+38% YoY) on volumes of 52,080 MT (+22% YoY), with EBITDA of INR100 crores (+82%) at a 12% margin and PAT of INR48 crores (+220%). H1 revenue was INR1,430 crores (+22%) on 92,809 MT (+7%), with EBITDA of INR177 crores (+86%) at 12%. Management attributed part of the volume growth to channel restocking after PVC prices firmed, plus consolidation as smaller players lost share, and said working capital improved with DSO falling to 34 days. Bathware (Aquel) posted revenue of INR19 crores and EBITDA of minus INR4 crores in the quarter.

financial_highlights.value: 55 days; receivable days 34; inventory days 74 (as of 30 Sep 2026)

segments.name: Bathware (Aquel)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR19 crores with EBITDA of minus INR4 crores. Management expects to be very close to breakeven in Q3 and breakeven in Q4, requiring about INR24-25 crores revenue per quarter; currently about INR20 crores per quarter.

segments.name: CPVC and PPR (value-added)
segments.commentary: Combined contribution now above 30% of revenue, up from close to 25% previously. CPVC is the fastest-growing polymer and grew faster than the industry, though no segment margins were disclosed.

segments.name: Project vs retail mix
segments.commentary: Project segment is around 25-30% of sales, with both retail and project growing.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume growth target is double-digit (previously guided 12-15%); this implies roughly 16-21% growth in H2 per an analyst's calculation, which management did not dispute.
EBITDA margin band of 11% to 13% maintained for the year, factoring in bathware expansion costs.
FY27 capex guidance of about INR200 crores retained; INR70 crores spent in H1 with the balance in H2.
FY28 capex mainly replacement and maintenance, estimated at INR100-120 crores; growth capex (debottlenecking, brownfield, greenfield) to follow after utilisation improves.
Receivable days targeted at 35-40 days and inventory at 70-80 days going forward.
PP (DECILO) manufacturing expansion at Silvassa planned by end of the March 2027 quarter.
CPVC raw material cost increase of 7-8% plus to be passed through to channel.
capex_capacity: Total installed capacity at H1 FY27 is 4,35,000 metric tons.
FY27 capex guidance around INR200 crores; INR70 crores spent in H1 FY27.
FY28 capex estimated at INR100-120 crores, covering process, extrusion and injection replacement and maintenance.
Bihar (Begusarai) plant showing strong capacity utilisation, ahead of management's plan; East freight and operating leverage benefits passed to channel.
DECILO polypropylene line to be added at Silvassa by end of March 2027 quarter; currently made at Haridwar.
demand_pricing: Demand described as healthy in end-product terms; restocking contributed to Q2 volumes as channel inventory was low at quarter start. October volume growth was on a low base (Diwali in October last year) but in line with Q2 trajectory.

PVC prices stabilised in the September quarter; government minimum import price (MIP) on PVC resin supports the floor. Management expects PVC range-bound at about INR95-100 per kg post-MIP and CVD, with limited downside.
Large-player competition described as no longer predatory; smaller players losing share through consolidation.
No inventory gain in Q2; management said any gain was passed to channel via a 7-10 day lag in price pass-through.
Management views 1.5-2% of sales as the consistent marketing spend; Kon Honar Crorepati sponsorship announced.
Company is deliberately avoiding infrastructure, government and OPVC segments, focusing on B2C and private real estate B2B.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 volume growth was restocking versus real demand, and is it sustainable into Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Part was restocking after PVC firmed, but management said distributors will keep higher inventory as the MIP sets a price floor; demand described as healthy, with consolidation as smaller players lose share.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses rise sharply over the last two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an actuarial valuation impact on salary cost, around 10% organisation-wide increase, and new sales force additions in new markets.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 12-15% volume growth guidance be met given H1 growth of 7.3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full-year double-digit volume growth is the target, dependent on a strong H2 and on share gains; capacity is already in place ahead of demand.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin hold at 12-12.5% or above?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed the 11-13% band, citing product mix and operating leverage, and said H1 gross margin delivery is sustainable with no inventory gain or loss assumed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to bathware breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven needs INR24-25 crores revenue per quarter; management expects close to breakeven in Q3 and breakeven by Q4, with South and East revenue starting in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Why pass on inventory gains to channel when demand is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pass-through was delayed by 7-10 days (about 1-2 weeks) to give channel breathing room after a steep cost increase, not a material change in policy.

risks_watch: Volume growth needs a sharp H2 acceleration (about 16-21% per an analyst's calculation) against H1 growth of 7%; Q2 included restocking effects.
PVC price path depends on MIP renewal or CVD implementation by the Finance Ministry; management cited 45-60 days from DGTR recommendation to implementation based on past precedent.
Bathware losses continue until Q4 at the earliest; breakeven depends on South and East ramp-up.
Receivable and inventory days targets (35-40 and 70-80) are forward-looking and dependent on channel discipline.
Payables are a function of procurement mix (domestic shorter credit, imports longer), so working-capital gains are partly contingent on sourcing.
CPVC raw material cost up 7-8% plus, to be passed through in the coming quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, market share gains and the 11-13% margin band, with specific numbers offered on capex, CPVC pricing and bathware timelines. Evasive on the scale of the H2 volume ramp and on the exact split of restocking versus end demand, and declined to give segment-level margins or dealer-channel growth figures.
key_quotes: We will stick to that band of 11% to 13% with good volume growth.
So we are not interested in one-off kind of inventory gains. We are more interested in sustainable volume growth, which is at a healthy kind of profitability.

adds.what: DECILO polypropylene line at Silvassa (moving production from Haridwar)

growth.why: FY27 volume growth guided to double digit (prior 12-15%), implying roughly 16-21% H2 growth per analyst math that management did not dispute; backing is partial (Bihar utilisation, Silvassa DECILO line by end-March 2027 quarter, FY27 capex ~INR200 crores with INR70 crores spent in H1), but no specific order book or capacity numbers were given to cover the H2 surge.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 12% in Q2 (+300 bps YoY) and H1 12%; management reaffirmed the 11-13% band citing mix and operating leverage, with CPVC and PPR now above 30% of revenue (up from ~25%) and bathware losses (EBITDA -INR4 crores on INR19 crores revenue) expected to reach breakeven by Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: DECILO polypropylene line at Silvassa planned by end of March 2027 quarter, moving production from Haridwar; installed capacity 4,35,000 MT and Bihar plant running at very strong utilisation, though the line is a minor addition to a large base.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets double-digit FY27 volume growth (cut from 12-15%), which implies roughly 16-21% H2 growth against H1 +7% per an analyst's math that management did not dispute; Q2's +22% was partly restocking and the company gave no order book or H2 volume numbers.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of about INR200 crores retained with INR70 crores spent in H1; FY28 capex estimated at INR100-120 crores mainly replacement, with growth capex (debottlenecking, brownfield, greenfield) to follow only after utilisation improves, so a new growth capex announcement is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Volume guidance was cut from 12-15% to double digit and the margin band of 11-13% was merely held, so management is not signalling a raise despite a 12% H1 margin.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Double-digit volume target needs a sharp H2 acceleration against H1 +7%, and the call said Q2 was helped by restocking, with PVC import-policy and bathware breakeven timing dependent on uncertain factors.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Only the DECILO polypropylene line at Silvassa is named (by end-March 2027 quarter); no other new products or brands were disclosed beyond CPVC and PPR growth already under way.

rows.label: Bathware (Aquel) breakeven
rows.why: Revenue of INR19 crores in Q2 with EBITDA of -INR4 crores; breakeven needs about INR24-25 crores per quarter versus INR20 crores now, with South and East ramp-up expected to close the gap, though management guided breakeven only in Q4.

rows.label: CPVC raw material pass-through
rows.why: CPVC raw material cost up 7-8% plus, which management plans to pass through to the channel, while PVC is expected range-bound at INR95-100 per kg post-MIP and CVD with limited downside.

rows.label: Receivable and inventory days targets
rows.why: Receivable days fell to 34 and H1 working-capital days are 55; targets of 35-40 receivable and 70-80 inventory days are guided, though payables depend on sourcing mix and channel discipline.
